 Order

The petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C for cancelling the non bailable warrant ('NBW' for short) and cancellation of bail by the Special Court in Spl.C.C.No.56/2020 dated 24.02.2023.

2. Heard the arguments of both the learned counsels.
3.
The case of the petitioner is that the petitioner facing the trial before the special Court as accused No.8 on various sections of the IPC and other offences.
She was regularly appearing before Trial Court and due to on medical emergency, she left the Country to U.K. for attending the medical treatment of her grand daughter.
The Exemption application came to be filed by the learned counsel, which was allowed for two occasions.

Later, NBW had been issued against the petitioner and subsequently, bond has been cancelled on 24.02.2023 on the ground that petitioner left to U.K without notice of Trial Court, which is under challenge.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits before canceling the bail and forfeiting the bond,
no notice has been issued to the surety and the petitioner herself stated in the Exemption application that she left U.K for her medical emergency.
The learned counsel produced the medical records stating that she has went to U.K on medical emergency Visa.

The learned counsel submits that the Trial Court without considering the same, cancelled the bail which reveals the petitioner was appearing before the Court, on many hearings she was continuously appearing and due to medical emergency she left the country for attending her grand daughter and the trial Court before canceling the bail could have issued notice to the surety calling for the explanation and there after should have cancelled the bail.
It was also noted that no condition imposed by the Trial Court, while granting bail that she should not leave the head quarters or country without prior permission.

Considering the same, when there is no condition imposed by the Trial Court for not to leave the head quarters for leave the country without prior permission, the question of canceling the bail, on the ground for violating the terms and bail does not arise.

The Trial Court ought to have issued Smt Sarita Sharma vs The State Of Karnataka on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198151206/
2 notice to the surety thereafter, proceeding with in accordance with law.
